title: M-CHAT-R (Modified Checklist for Autism in Toddlers, Revised)

low_risk.description: Low Risk - No further action required unless surveillance indicates risk

moderate_risk.description: Moderate Risk - Refer for diagnostic evaluation

high_risk.description: High Risk - Immediate referral for diagnostic evaluation

questions.text: If you point at something across the room, does your child look at it?

examples.pass: Child looks across room at toy/object when parent points
examples.fail: Child looks at parent's hand instead of object, or ignores pointing

questions.text: Have you ever wondered if your child might be deaf?

examples.pass: Parent has never had concerns about hearing
examples.fail: Parent has wondered if child is deaf due to lack of response to name/sounds

questions.text: Does your child play pretend or make-believe?

examples.pass: Pretends to feed doll, talks on toy phone, pretends to cook
examples.fail: Only lines up toys, spins wheels, no imaginative scenarios

questions.text: Does your child like climbing on things?

examples.pass: Climbs on furniture, playground equipment, stairs
examples.fail: Avoids climbing, seems afraid or uninterested

questions.text: Does your child make unusual finger movements near his or her eyes?

examples.pass: No unusual finger movements near eyes
examples.fail: Wiggles fingers close to eyes, looks at hands from unusual angles

questions.text: Does your child point with one finger to ask for something or to get help?

examples.pass: Points with index finger to request food, toy, help
examples.fail: Uses whole hand, leads adult by hand, doesn't point

questions.text: Does your child point with one finger to show you something interesting?

examples.pass: Points to airplane, dog, interesting object to share experience
examples.fail: Doesn't point to share, only points for requests or not at all

questions.text: Is your child interested in other children?

examples.pass: Watches other children, tries to play near them, excited to see peers
examples.fail: Ignores other children, prefers to play alone, indifferent

questions.text: Does your child show you things by bringing them to you or holding them up for you to see?

examples.pass: Brings toy to show parent, holds up picture for parent to see
examples.fail: Plays alone, doesn't share objects or experiences

questions.text: Does your child respond when you call his or her name?

examples.pass: Looks up, turns toward parent when name is called
examples.fail: Ignores name most of the time, needs multiple calls

questions.text: When you smile at your child, does he or she smile back at you?

examples.pass: Returns smile, shares enjoyment through facial expression
examples.fail: Rarely smiles back, flat affect, doesn't engage

questions.text: Does your child get upset by everyday noises?

examples.pass: Tolerates normal household sounds without distress
examples.fail: Covers ears, cries with vacuum, blender, hand dryers

questions.text: Does your child walk?

examples.pass: Walks independently
examples.fail: Not yet walking by screening age

questions.text: Does your child look you in the eye when you are talking to him or her, playing with him or her, or dressing him or her?

examples.pass: Makes eye contact during interactions, conversations
examples.fail: Avoids eye contact, looks past people, fleeting gaze

questions.text: Does your child try to copy what you do?

examples.pass: Copies clapping, waving, cleaning, actions with objects
examples.fail: Doesn't imitate gestures or actions, ignores demonstrations

questions.text: If you turn your head to look at something, does your child look around to see what you are looking at?

examples.pass: Follows parent's gaze to look at same object/event
examples.fail: Doesn't notice where parent is looking, doesn't follow gaze

questions.text: Does your child try to get you to watch him or her?

examples.pass: Says 'look at me', performs for attention, seeks approval
examples.fail: Doesn't seek attention, plays independently without checking in

questions.text: Does your child understand when you tell him or her to do something?

examples.pass: Follows simple commands like 'get your shoes', 'sit down'
examples.fail: Doesn't respond to instructions without gestures

questions.text: If something new happens, does your child look at your face to see how you feel about it?

examples.pass: Looks to parent when stranger arrives, new toy appears
examples.fail: Doesn't check parent's reaction in new situations

questions.text: Does your child like movement activities?

examples.pass: Enjoys being swung, bounced, rough-and-tumble play
examples.fail: Avoids movement, gets upset when picked up, dislikes swinging
